name: Creatine
description: TSA powder rules for flying with creatine, protein powder, and workout supplements in carry-on and checked luggage.

carryOn.reason: Creatine powder is allowed in carry-on bags. However, under the TSA powder rule, powder containers exceeding 12 oz (350 ml) must be placed in a separate bin for X-ray screening and may be subject to additional inspection.
conditions: Containers over 12 oz (350 ml / roughly the size of a standard soda can) must be removed from your bag and placed in a dedicated bin.
TSA officers may open the container to perform chemical residue or test swab screening.
Powders that cannot be resolved through secondary screening may be denied boarding.
exceptions: Creatine pills, capsules, and gummies are treated as solid items and exempt from the powder bin rule.

checkedBag.reason: Creatine powder and all fitness supplements are fully allowed in checked baggage without size limits or special checkpoint screening.
conditions: Seal container securely to prevent powder spillage inside your luggage during pressure changes.

tsa.pageTitle: Can I bring creatine on a plane?

airlines.name: American Airlines
airlines.notes: Powder supplements permitted in carry-on (subject to 12 oz screening) and checked bags.

airlines.name: Emirates
airlines.notes: Creatine and nutritional powders allowed in cabin and checked luggage.

international.note: International flights departing to the US (and countries following ICAO guidelines like Australia and New Zealand) enforce the 350g powder limit strictly at boarding gates.

travelTips: Keep creatine in its original labeled container so TSA agents can quickly verify the supplement ingredients.
If traveling with a large tub (over 12 oz), pack it in your checked luggage to speed through security checkpoints.
Pre-portion daily servings in labeled ziplock bags or a pill organizer for short weekend trips.

faq.question: Can I bring creatine powder through TSA airport security?
faq.answer: Yes! Creatine powder is 100% permitted in carry-on bags. If your container is larger than 12 oz (350 ml), place it in a separate bin at the security checkpoint for X-ray and possible swab inspection.

faq.question: Does creatine need to be in its original container?
faq.answer: While not strictly required by TSA law, keeping creatine in its original manufacturer-sealed container with nutrition label dramatically reduces the chance of secondary chemical testing or questioning.

faq.question: Is creatine allowed in checked luggage?
faq.answer: Yes. There are no size limits or special screening procedures for creatine powder in checked baggage. You can pack full tubs without issue.
